summary: SapphireLine multi-region routing race caused streaming truncation during end-of-day batches — customer escalation and action plan
description:
Issue summary:
During SapphireLine's nightly end-of-day batch (scheduled 02:00-03:30 UTC), a subset of inference requests experienced streaming truncation and intermittent 5xx spikes across us-east and eu-west. Customers reported partial transcripts and missing trailing tokens for streaming completions, plus repeated client reconnects. Impact: multiple business-critical batch jobs failed to reconcile logs and generated duplicate downstream processing attempts.

Impact:
- Affected ~7% of batch traffic for SapphireLine between 2026-03-11 02:07 and 2026-03-11 02:41 UTC.
- Streaming responses truncated mid-completion; clients saw final chunk missing.
- Several retries caused billing/usage anomalies and duplicate downstream webhooks.

Environment:
- Hosted Redwood API (enterprise tenant), dedicated routing for SapphireLine in us-east and eu-west.
- Smart-router service v2.3.1 deployed across both regions.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Run high-concurrency streaming job against redwood/gptx-13b-v2 with session affinity enabled and target traffic split across two availability zones.
2) Trigger a control-plane autoscaler event that drains one routing pool (simulated node removal).
3) Observe some streams where the handshake completes but the stream ends with no terminal chunk; client reconnects and receives a truncated resume offset.

Logs & traces:
- Correlation IDs attached in investigation notes.
- Streaming proxy logs show abrupt TCP FIN from nodes receiving requests after routing table change.
- Smart-router trace shows concurrent topology update and in-flight route reassignment in a 350ms window.
comments: 2026-03-11 02:18 - SapphireLine SRE (customer): 'We're seeing hundreds of truncated streaming completions in the EOD flush. It's causing reconciliation to drop the last line item. Can you confirm this is on your side?'
2026-03-11 02:21 - Support (Aisha): 'Acknowledged — investigating. We've opened a Major Incident and are pulling SRE/Serving on-call. ETA for first update 10 minutes.'

2026-03-11 02:31 - SRE (Liam): 'Preliminary: smart-router v2.3.1 performed a topology update while autoscaler issued drain signals. Some in-flight streams were redirected to nodes without the streaming plugin enabled (legacy-quant routing path) and the stream frame API returned early EOFs.'

2026-03-11 02:44 - Support (Aisha): 'Mitigation: rolled back smart-router to v2.3.0 in us-east and eu-west for SapphireLine's routes. Re-routed live traffic to stable pool. Customer reporting improved behaviour — truncated responses no longer observed after 02:42 UTC.'

2026-03-11 09:12 - SapphireLine Engineering: 'Thanks for the quick response. We did see jobs clear and our reconciliation completed for the remaining batches. Please advise on permanent mitigations and billing credits for duplicate downstream webhooks.'
2026-03-12 16:05 - Product (Lydia Chen): 'Documenting follow-ups: smart-router release gating, add e2e streaming resume tests, and ensure autoscaler drain window is extended for streaming workloads.'
investigation_notes: Observation 1: The timing window where topology update overlapped with drain events was ~350ms; requests launched in that window were marked routed to new node but had backend handshake discrepancies.

Observation 2: Legacy routing path (metric name: routing.plugin.legacy_quant) lacked the streaming-frame-seq header enforcement introduced in 2.3.0 — result: resumed connections lacked monotonic seq and were treated as new streams.

Hypothesis: race in control-plane (smart-router v2.3.1) plus aggressive autoscaler drain timeout caused some streams to be reassigned mid-session to nodes missing streaming plugin; clients received early EOF and retried, producing duplicate downstream webhook events.

Evidence: tcpdump + streaming-proxy logs show FIN from reassigned nodes and subsequent new connections with identical client session-id but starting sequence at 0; correlation IDs show truncated transcript length matches shard assignment changes.
Timeline: 02:07 UTC first truncated stream observed; 02:18 customer escalation; 02:31 engineering identified routing race; 02:36 rollback started; 02:42 stable behaviour restored for affected routes.
Related telemetry: token-level cost spike correlating to retries between 02:10-02:45 UTC; approximate billing delta for SapphireLine ~0.9% of that day's usage (to be reconciled).
resolution:
Immediate mitigation:
- Rolled back smart-router to v2.3.0 for SapphireLine routes in us-east and eu-west (02:36-02:40 UTC).
- Re-routed traffic to stable serving pool and disabled aggressive autoscale drains for streaming tenant for 24 hours.

Permanent fixes planned / completed:
- Hotfix (deployed 2026-03-12): smart-router v2.3.2 with serialized topology apply and a streaming-plugin capability negotiation step to prevent routing to nodes without streaming support.
- Added monotonic sequence header enforcement for streaming resume so resumed streams are validated and duplicates are rejected.
- Autoscaler change: extend drain window by default for streaming workloads and add a drain-safe flag for routes with active streaming sessions.

Customer remediation & follow-up:
- Issued a 30% invoice credit for the affected billing window and committed to a dedicated post-incident review with SapphireLine engineering.
- Action items assigned: engineering to add e2e streaming failover tests in CI; SRE to add a dashboard alert for topology-change-in-flight > 100ms; support to coordinate with billing to reconcile webhook duplication charges.
- Post-incident exec brief scheduled 2026-03-16 with product, SRE, and SapphireLine (invite sent).
